answer: Each identity claims a unique point in a public embedding map, and claims that sit too close are merged into one vote. Each epoch the holder must take a small, recorded step into a still-unoccupied neighboring region, leaving a spiral of occupancy no other key may share. A dune of packed clones collapses to a single point. A late or colliding step counts as a failed whisper and earns nothing, so a farm cannot keep thousands of well-separated paths moving without overlaps or silence.
